[BAYDAWI-FULL:2:180/r12] BAYDAWI-FULL, d. 685 · author | reports | To avoid conflict, al-waṣiyya may mean God’s command that parents and relatives inherit, or the dying person’s allocation of what God prescribed for them.

[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p155/r3] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · author | holds | The will verse follows naturally after the discussion of killing, retaliation, and blood money: it alerts each person to make a will before sudden death.
[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p155/r4] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · author | rejects | There is no need to coordinate this clause with the earlier command about retaliation or posit a deleted conjunction; it is a new sentence clearly connected in meaning to what precedes.
[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p155/r5] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · author | holds | The author's preferred sense of death's arrival is the arrival of its precursors and causes, such as illness and alarming symptoms; Arabic usage metaphorically calls causes of death death.
[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p155/r6] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · author | holds | The Qurʾānic phrase about death coming from every place while the person is not dead and the cited poems use death for its causes or personify death; Antarah, Jarir, and an unnamed poet provide examples. | mentions 14:17
[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p155/r7] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · author | holds | The plural address means each believer individually, then the clause switches to one of you; the expected plural was avoided by following the universal sense of upon you, a rare construction illustrated by poetry.
[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p157/r1] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · قول غير مسمى | reports | An alternative takes death literally and addresses executors and heirs: when someone dies they must carry out the will; on this reading the verse itself does not prove that making a will is obligatory.
[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p157/r10] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · علي | reports | ʿAli stopped a client with seven hundred from making a will, saying that this did not count as wealth under the verse.
[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p157/r11] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · author | holds | The lack of a fixed amount does not negate obligation: the apparent rule applies once any wealth exists; if khayr has a narrower sense, juristic judgment determines what qualifies as good and sufficient wealth.
[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p157/r12] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · author | holds | Calling the estate khayr subtly implies that it is lawful wealth: illicit property must be returned to its owners, and making a will from it is sinful.
[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p157/r13] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · قول غير مسمى | reports | One view holds the verse operative and makes a bequest to parents and relatives obligatory alongside their inheritance under the two verses. | mentions 4:11
[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p157/r14] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · قول غير مسمى | reports | Another view considers the verse operative but understands it to recommend voluntary bequests.
[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p157/r15] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · قول غير مسمى | reports | A further view says the will command does not conflict with inheritance; it concerns God's assignment of parents' and relatives' shares. | mentions 4:11
[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p157/r2] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · مجاهد | reports | Mujahid says khayr means wealth throughout the Qurʾān, citing its uses for wealth in several other passages. | mentions 100:8, 38:32, 24:33, 12:93
[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p157/r3] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · الزهري وأبو مجلز | reports | They take the apparent wording to mean any amount of wealth, so a will is due whether the estate is small or large.

[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p157/r7] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · الجصاص | reports | Al-Jaṣṣāṣ sets the threshold at four thousand dirhams.

[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p158/r5] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · ابن عمر وابن عباس وابن زيد | reports | They regard the entire verse as abrogated; the bequest remains recommended, a position also attributed to al-Shaʿbi, al-Nakhaʿi, and Malik.
[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p158/r6] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · الربيع بن خثيم وغيره | reports | Al-Rabiʿ ibn Khuthaym and others are reported as holding that there is no bequest.

[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p158/r8] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · قول غير مسمى | reports | One position gives relatives first claim on bequests and bars a bequest to outsiders when relatives are left without one.
[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p158/r9] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · الشعبي | rejects | When Abu al-ʿAliya left his estate to Banu Hashim despite having been freed by a woman of Riyah, al-Shaʿbi objected that he had no right to do so.
[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p159/r1] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · أبو ثور | reports | Abu Thawr says a will is obligatory only for someone with a debt or property entrusted by others; it is not obligatory for someone with neither.
[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p159/r10] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · ابن وهب عن مالك | reports | Ibn Wahb reports that heirs may withdraw consent given in good health but not consent given during illness; al-Layth agrees with Malik, and jurists agree that approval after death cannot be revoked.
[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p159/r11] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · طاووس وعطاء | reports | Tawus and ʿAtaʾ hold that heirs' approval during the testator's life is binding.

[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p159/r13] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · أبو حنيفة | reports | Abu Hanifa rejects a minor's will; al-Muzani says this follows by analogy from al-Shafiʿi, while Malik and others permit it.

[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p159/r2] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · قول غير مسمى | reports | Another view denies that making a will is obligatory, citing al-Nakhaʿi's report that the Prophet died without making one and a hadith that conditions it on wanting to make a will.

[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p159/r5] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · مالك | reports | If the testator directs that a bequest to an heir go to God's cause unless the heirs approve it, Malik says it becomes part of the estate when they refuse.
[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p159/r6] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · أبو حنيفة ومعمر | reports | They say the refused bequest in that arrangement is spent in God's cause.
[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p159/r7] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · ابن أبي ليلى وعثمان البتي | reports | They hold that if heirs approve an outsider's bequest above one third during the testator's life, they cannot revoke that approval after death.
[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p159/r8] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · أبو حنيفة ومحمد وأبو يوسف وزفر والحسن بن صالح وعبيد الله بن الحسن | reports | They require heirs to renew their approval after death; consent given during the testator's life alone is ineffective, a view also reported from ʿAbd Allah, Shurayh, and Ibrahim.

[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p160/r1] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · مالك وأبو حنيفة | reports | Malik and Abu Hanifa say an owner cannot revoke a mudabbar arrangement; al-Shafiʿi, Ahmad, Ishaq, al-Shaʿbi, al-Nakhaʿi, Ibn Shubruma, and al-Thawri treat it as a will.

[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p160/r4] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · الشافعي وأحمد وإسحاق وأبو ثور | reports | They classify all these formulations as wills.
[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p160/r5] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · أبو ثور | reports | Abu Thawr says the declaration I have revoked my mudabbar cancels the arrangement; al-Shafiʿi requires an actual sale or gift, since merely saying I revoke is ineffective.
[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p160/r6] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · ابن القاسم وأشهب | reports | For the ambiguous statement that a slave will be free after the owner's death without expressly intending a will or manumission arrangement, Ibn al-Qasim calls it a will and Ashhab calls it a mudabbar.
[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p160/r7] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · الدارقطني عن أنس بن مالك | reports | A testament formula used by the righteous predecessors confesses God's oneness, Muhammad's messengership, the Hour and resurrection, then exhorts one's family to fear God, reconcile, and obey God and His Messenger; it invokes Abraham's and Jacob's counsel to their children to die as Muslims.
[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p160/r8] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · أنس بن مالك | reports | Al-Daraqutni transmits the cited testament formula from Anas ibn Malik.
[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p160/r9] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · author | holds | Kataba is passive, with its agent omitted because God is known to be meant and for brevity; al-waṣiyya is apparently the passive subject, and the feminine verb lacks agreement because of separation, length, nonhuman feminine gender, and the sense of bequeathing.
[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p161/r1] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · author | holds | The second condition has an omitted answer indicated by the first omitted answer, so the omitted answer in turn indicates another omission; the author calls the combined conditional structure one of the hardest syntax problems and refers readers to al-Takmil.
[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p161/r2] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · قول غير مسمى | reports | Another parse treats both answers as omitted, understands kataba as future-directed obligation, and makes idha a temporal adverb governed by kataba; the answer to if he leaves wealth is then also omitted and signaled by kataba.

[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p162/r2] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · الزمخشري | reports | Al-Zamakhshari calls al-waṣiyya the faʿil of kataba, his term for the passive subject, and explains the masculine verb by separation and by the sense of the verbal phrase to make a will.
[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p162/r3] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · قول غير مسمى | reports | Some grammarians make al-waṣiyya a subject in a conditional answer, with an omitted fa or an implied predicate such as it is due; the passive subject would be an implicit yuktabu explained by the wording that follows.
[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p162/r4] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · author | rejects | Abū Ḥayyān again finds Ibn ʿAṭiyya's analysis inconsistent: if idha is governed as a temporal adverb it is not a condition, and an omitted passive subject or unspoken verbal noun cannot serve as the proposed governor under the stated Basran rules.
[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p163#2/r1] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · author | prefers | The prepositional phrase serving as passive subject is the best analysis and requires fewer assumptions than positing an implicit verbal noun and its pronoun.
[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p163#2/r10] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · قول غير مسمى | reports | Another interpretation requires that the bequest concern a known portion of the testator's property rather than an unspecified amount.
[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p163#2/r11] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · الزمخشري | reports | Al-Zamakhshari summarizes fairness as justice: do not leave the poor for the rich and do not exceed one third.
[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p163#2/r12] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · author | holds | The phrase bi-l-maʿrūf attaches either to al-waṣiyya or to an omitted adjective meaning characterized by fairness, making it a circumstantial phrase.
[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p163#2/r13] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · ابن عطية والزمخشري | reports | Ibn ʿAṭiyya and al-Zamakhshari parse ḥaqqan as an emphatic verbal noun affirming the sentence's content, roughly this is truly binding.
[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p163#2/r14] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · author | rejects | Abū Ḥayyān rejects that parse because the following phrase ʿalā al-muttaqīn must attach to ḥaqqan or describe it, which prevents ḥaqqan from being an emphatic verbal noun under the grammatical rules he cites.
[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p163#2/r2] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · author | holds | The author says the phrase about parents was discussed earlier in the command to show kindness to parents. | mentions 2:83
[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p163#2/r3] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · author | holds | Al-aqrabīn is the plural of al-aqrab, an elative meaning nearest; its apparent scope includes every relative closer to the deceased, with parents named first and then included again for emphasis and special care.
[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p163#2/r4] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · المفسرون | reports | Exegetes identify the relatives variously as children, relatives other than children, all kin, or non-inheriting relatives.
[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p163#2/r5] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · قول غير مسمى | reports | One explanation of fairness limits a bequest to one third and says not to favor the rich over the poor.
[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p163#2/r6] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · ابن مسعود | reports | Ibn Masʿud explains fairness as giving first to the neediest relative.
[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p163#2/r7] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · قول غير مسمى | reports | Another explanation is that the will must contain no injustice.
[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p163#2/r8] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · قول غير مسمى | reports | Another view initially leaves the amount to the testator's judgment, then sets the upper limit at one third, citing the report that one third is much.
[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p163#2/r9] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · قول غير مسمى | reports | Fairness may mean a moderate amount recognized by people's conscience without harming heirs, since people had sometimes bequeathed all their property.
[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p163/r1] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · author | rejects | Ibn ʿAṭiyya misquotes Sibawayh's supporting verse; Sibawayh actually cites the line beginning whoever does good deeds, God rewards them, and says this construction is only poetic necessity.
[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p163/r2] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · سيبويه عن الخليل | holds | Sibawayh transmits al-Khalil's ruling that a conditional clause without fa, such as if you come to me, I am generous, occurs only when a poet is forced; al-Akhfash's implied-fa analysis is refuted by this evidence.
[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p163/r3] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · author | prefers | The less strained parse makes the prepositional phrase ʿalaykum the passive subject: al-waṣiyya then answers the listener's implicit question about what was prescribed, as subject or predicate.
[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p170/r3] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · author | holds | The passage prescribes a deathbed will, threatens those who knowingly alter it, and exempts reconciliation among recipients when the testator's will was biased or wrongful.
[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p170/r4] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · author | holds | These verses frame the accountable person's life from faith in God at its beginning to the will at death, with major duties and sins selected as examples rather than an exhaustive list.
[SAMIN-DURR:2:180#2/r1] SAMIN-DURR, d. 756 · ابن عطية | reports | Ibn Atiyya lets an implied الإيصاء govern إذا and makes الوصية a مبتدأ; the implicit answer is like فعليه الوصية with a deleted فاء.
[SAMIN-DURR:2:180#2/r2] SAMIN-DURR, d. 756 · سيبويه | reports | Ibn Atiyya invokes Sibawayh's conditional verse example, من يفعل الصالحات الله يحفظه, with the answer's فاء omitted.
[SAMIN-DURR:2:180#2/r3] SAMIN-DURR, d. 756 · author | rejects | The author objects that if implied الإيصاء governs إذا, it is purely temporal and cannot have a conditional answer; an omitted or implicit مصدر cannot govern under Basran rules or be deleted as نائب الفاعل.
[SAMIN-DURR:2:180#2/r4] SAMIN-DURR, d. 756 · author | rejects | A single clause cannot answer both إن and إذا; each condition requires its own answer.
[SAMIN-DURR:2:180#2/r5] SAMIN-DURR, d. 756 · سيبويه | reports | Sibawayh permits deleting فاء جواب only by poetic necessity, citing a line where الله يشكرها follows the conditional.
[SAMIN-DURR:2:180#2/r6] SAMIN-DURR, d. 756 · المبرد | reports | Al-Mubarrad reportedly forbids deleting فاء even in poetry and transmits فالرحمن يشكره; others say this does not refute Sibawayh's transmitted wording.
[SAMIN-DURR:2:180#2/r7] SAMIN-DURR, d. 756 · author | prefers | The preferred parse estimates إن ترك خيرا فليوص; that omitted answer also indicates the answer to إذا, better than making one condition answer another or reinterpreting كتب.
[SAMIN-DURR:2:180#3/r1] SAMIN-DURR, d. 756 · author | reports | الوصية may be a مبتدأ with للوالدين as its predicate.
[SAMIN-DURR:2:180#3/r2] SAMIN-DURR, d. 756 · author | reports | Alternatively الوصية is the object and نائب الفاعل of كتب.
[SAMIN-DURR:2:180#3/r3] SAMIN-DURR, d. 756 · الأخفش | rejects | A third parse makes الوصية a مبتدأ with omitted predicate فعليه; the author says al-Akhfash's permission to drop فاء جواب is refuted by Sibawayh's transmission.
[SAMIN-DURR:2:180#3/r4] SAMIN-DURR, d. 756 · author | reports | بالمعروف may attach to الوصية or be a circumstantial qualifier through an omitted phrase: the bequest is fair, not unjust.
[SAMIN-DURR:2:180#4/r1] SAMIN-DURR, d. 756 · author | reports | حقا may modify an omitted مصدر of كتب or أوصى, meaning a true writing or bequest.
[SAMIN-DURR:2:180#4/r2] SAMIN-DURR, d. 756 · author | reports | Alternatively حقا is a circumstantial accusative from the definite omitted مصدر of كتب or أوصى.
[SAMIN-DURR:2:180#4/r3] SAMIN-DURR, d. 756 · الزمخشري وابن عطية وأبو البقاء | reports | Al-Zamakhshari, Ibn Atiyya, and Abu al-Baqa take حقا as emphasis of the sentence's content, with omitted عامل حق ذلك حقا.
[SAMIN-DURR:2:180#4/r4] SAMIN-DURR, d. 756 · author | rejects | The author objects that attaching على المتقين to an emphatic مصدر violates its inability to govern, while making it an adjective undermines emphasis.
[SAMIN-DURR:2:180#4/r5] SAMIN-DURR, d. 756 · بعض المعربين | rejects | Some grammarians attach حقا to the meaning of المتقين, like الأنفال 74; the author objects that it precedes its relative عامل and is unnatural. | mentions 8:74
[SAMIN-DURR:2:180#4/r6] SAMIN-DURR, d. 756 · author | prefers | The author prefers حقا as a verbal noun from the meaning of كتب: كتب الوصية means it became due, like قعدت جلوسا.
[SAMIN-DURR:2:180/r1] SAMIN-DURR, d. 756 · author | holds | كتب is passive; its omitted agent is God, understood from context and left out for brevity.
[SAMIN-DURR:2:180/r2] SAMIN-DURR, d. 756 · author | reports | One نائب الفاعل parse makes الوصية the subject; its feminine is metaphorical, and separation permits the masculine verb.
[SAMIN-DURR:2:180/r3] SAMIN-DURR, d. 756 · author | reports | Another نائب الفاعل parse takes الوصية to imply الإيصاء, the verbal noun understood as what was prescribed.
[SAMIN-DURR:2:180/r4] SAMIN-DURR, d. 756 · الأخفش والكوفيون | reports | Al-Akhfash and the Kufans allow the prepositional phrase as نائب الفاعل: عليكم is nominative on this parse and accusative on the other two.
[SAMIN-DURR:2:180/r5] SAMIN-DURR, d. 756 · author | holds | The author makes كتب govern إذا as a purely temporal adverb, not a condition: the prescription applies at death's arrival.

[IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p492#2/r1] IBNKATHIR-FULL, d. 774 · author | holds | On the stronger of two views, bequests to parents and relatives were obligatory before the inheritance verses; fixed inheritance shares abrogated the duty for heirs, who now take their divinely set shares without a bequest or the testator's favor.
[IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p492#2/r2] IBNKATHIR-FULL, d. 774 · النبي | reports | The Prophet says God has given each rights-holder their due, so an heir may not receive a bequest.
[IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p492#2/r3] IBNKATHIR-FULL, d. 774 · ابن عباس | reports | After reciting the verse, Ibn Abbas said it had been abrogated; al-Hakim graded this report authentic on the two authorities' criteria.
[IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p492#2/r4] IBNKATHIR-FULL, d. 774 · ابن عباس | reports | Ibn Abbas says that initially only parents inherited alongside one another, while other relatives received by bequest; the inheritance verse set the parents' shares and preserved a bequest for relatives from one-third of the estate.
[IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p492#2/r5] IBNKATHIR-FULL, d. 774 · ابن عباس | reports | Ibn Abbas, via Ata, says this bequest verse was abrogated by the inheritance ruling in 4:7. | mentions 4:7
[IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p492#2/r6] IBNKATHIR-FULL, d. 774 · ابن عمر وأبو موسى وسعيد بن المسيب والحسن ومجاهد وعطاء وسعيد بن جبير | reports | Ibn Abi Hatim lists Ibn Umar, Abu Musa, Saʿid ibn al-Musayyib, Hasan, Mujahid, Ata, and Saʿid ibn Jubayr as holding that inheritance verses abrogated this verse.
[IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p492#2/r7] IBNKATHIR-FULL, d. 774 · محمد بن سيرين وعكرمة وزيد بن أسلم والربيع بن أنس وقتادة والسدي ومقاتل بن حيان | reports | Ibn Abi Hatim also lists Ibn Sirin, Ikrima, Zayd ibn Aslam, al-Rabi, Qatada, al-Suddi, and Muqatil ibn Hayyan as holding that inheritance verses abrogated this verse.
[IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p492#2/r8] IBNKATHIR-FULL, d. 774 · طاوس وإبراهيم النخعي وشريح والضحاك والزهري | reports | Ibn Abi Hatim also lists Tawus, Ibrahim al-Nakhaʿi, Shurayh, al-Dahhak, and al-Zuhri as holding that inheritance verses abrogated this verse.
[IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p493/r1] IBNKATHIR-FULL, d. 774 · أبو مسلم الأصفهاني | reports | Abu Muslim says the verse was not abrogated but explains inheritance legislation, glossing it as God's prescription for inheriting parents and relatives under 4:11; al-Razi says this is the view of most commentators and recognized jurists, which Ibn Kathir finds surprising. | mentions 4:11
[IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p493/r2] IBNKATHIR-FULL, d. 774 · ابن عباس والحسن ومسروق وطاوس والضحاك ومسلم بن يسار والعلاء بن زياد | reports | A reported middle view abrogates bequests for relatives who inherit but preserves them for those who do not; Ibn Abbas, Hasan, Masruq, Tawus, al-Dahhak, Muslim ibn Yasar, and al-Ala ibn Ziyad hold it.
[IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p493/r3] IBNKATHIR-FULL, d. 774 · سعيد بن جبير والربيع بن أنس وقتادة ومقاتل بن حيان | reports | Ibn Kathir adds Saʿid ibn Jubayr, al-Rabi, Qatada, and Muqatil ibn Hayyan to those holding that bequests were abrogated for heirs but remained for non-heirs.
[IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p493/r4] IBNKATHIR-FULL, d. 774 · author | holds | In later technical usage, the partial view is specification, not abrogation: inheritance law removes heirs from the general term relatives while non-inheriting relatives remain covered; this fits those who regard the original bequest as recommended.
[IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p493/r5] IBNKATHIR-FULL, d. 774 · author | prefers | Because the verse's context indicates an obligatory bequest, the author sides with the majority: bequests to inheriting relatives are abrogated by inheritance law and forbidden by the no-bequest-for-an-heir hadith.
[IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p493/r6] IBNKATHIR-FULL, d. 774 · author | holds | Inheritance law is an independent divine obligation for fixed-share heirs and residuaries, replacing the earlier ruling; bequests for non-inheriting relatives remain recommended from one-third, supported by this verse and the Prophet's instruction to keep a written will.
[IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p493/r7] IBNKATHIR-FULL, d. 774 · النبي | reports | The Prophet says a Muslim with something to bequeath should not spend two nights without a written will; Ibn Umar says he always kept one after hearing this.
[IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p494#2/r1] IBNKATHIR-FULL, d. 774 · author | holds | Maʿruf means gentle and benevolent treatment; Hasan says a bequest at death according to what is proper, not objectionable, is a Muslim's right.
[IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p494#2/r2] IBNKATHIR-FULL, d. 774 · الحسن | reports | Hasan says every Muslim should make a proper, non-objectionable bequest when death approaches.
[IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p494#2/r3] IBNKATHIR-FULL, d. 774 · author | holds | A proper bequest for relatives must not wrong heirs through extravagance or stinginess.
[IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p494#2/r4] IBNKATHIR-FULL, d. 774 · النبي | reports | When Saʿd, whose only heir was a daughter, asked to bequeath two-thirds or half his wealth, the Prophet refused; he allowed one-third but called it much, saying it is better to leave heirs wealthy than begging.
[IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p494#2/r5] IBNKATHIR-FULL, d. 774 · ابن عباس | reports | Ibn Abbas recommends reducing a bequest to a quarter rather than a third, citing the Prophet's statement that one-third is much.
[IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p494#2/r6] IBNKATHIR-FULL, d. 774 · النبي | reports | Hanifa bequeathed one hundred camels to an orphan in his care; when his sons complained, the Prophet limited a charitable bequest through stepped amounts from five to forty camels.
[IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p494/r1] IBNKATHIR-FULL, d. 774 · author | holds | Many verses and hadiths command kindness and benevolence toward relatives.
[IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p494/r2] IBNKATHIR-FULL, d. 774 · النبي | reports | A report from the Prophet has God tell Adam's child that He granted a share of wealth at death to purify him and His servants' prayer follows after death.
[IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p494/r3] IBNKATHIR-FULL, d. 774 · author | holds | Here khayr means wealth; Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, Ata, Saʿid ibn Jubayr, Abu al-Aliya, Atiyya al-Awfi, al-Dahhak, al-Suddi, al-Rabi, Muqatil ibn Hayyan, Qatada, and others are cited for this gloss.
[IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p494/r4] IBNKATHIR-FULL, d. 774 · author | reports | Authorities differ on whether a bequest applies regardless of the estate's size or only when substantial wealth is left.

[IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p496/r1] IBNKATHIR-FULL, d. 774 · author | holds | The author doubts that the camel-bequest report is reliably attributable to the Prophet.

[IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p58/r1] IBNKATHIR-FULL, d. 774 · عبد الله بن أبي أوفى | reports | Asked whether the Prophet made a will, Abdullah ibn Abi Awfa answered no; when asked how the commanded will was fulfilled, he said the Prophet willed the Book of God. | mentions 2:180
[IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p58/r2] IBNKATHIR-FULL, d. 774 · ابن عباس | reports | Ibn Kathir likens this to Ibn Abbas’s statement that the Prophet left only what lies between the two covers.
[IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p58/r3] IBNKATHIR-FULL, d. 774 · author | holds | People were required to bequeath their property when death approached, as stated in this verse.

[BIQAI-FULL:v1p333/r7] BIQAI-FULL, d. 885 · author | holds | After urging the giving of wealth and then life through retaliation, the passage urges bequest of wealth near death, when worldly poverty is no longer feared and afterlife reward is hoped for.

[BIQAI-FULL:v1p335/r4] BIQAI-FULL, d. 885 · author | holds | The emphasis in ḥaqqan and ʿalā al-muttaqīn stirs hearers to obey and reminds them of their coming account before God.
